summary.text: Covariance is a measure of how two random variables vary together, a joint variability.
It is positive when the variables tend to show similar behavior and negative when they tend to show opposite behavior.
Changing the units changes its value, so the correlation coefficient rescales it to a number between -1 and 1.

facts.label: Positive sign
facts.value: The variables tend to show similar behavior

facts.label: Negative sign
facts.value: The variables tend to show opposite behavior

facts.label: Units
facts.value: Units of X times units of Y

facts.label: Correlation range
facts.value: The normalized version lies between -1 and 1

items.prompt: On hot days a shop sells more ice cream, and on cold days it sells less. What is the sign of the covariance between temperature and sales?

options.label: Negative, as the two don't match
Zero, as temperature isn't a number
It has no sign at all
Positive, as they move in the same way

items.explain: Covariance is positive when two variables tend to show similar behavior.

items.prompt: A researcher measures the heights of some people in meters and then recomputes the covariance with weight after switching heights to millimeters. What happens?

options.label: The covariance value changes in proportion
The covariance is exactly the same
The covariance turns negative
The covariance always becomes zero

items.explain: Changing units changes the covariance value proportionally, which is why it is hard to judge the strength of a relationship from covariance alone.

items.prompt: Two variables have a covariance of exactly zero. Does it follow that they are independent?

options.label: Yes, zero means no link of any kind
Yes, it only happens when they are unrelated
No, they could be linked in a non-linear way
No, it means one is constant

items.explain: Covariance measures linear dependence, so uncorrelated variables need not be independent.

items.prompt: You want to compare how strongly two pairs of variables go together, but one pair is in dollars and the other in kilograms. What should you use?

options.label: The correlation coefficient
Whichever covariance is larger
The sum of the two covariances
The sample size of each pair

items.explain: The correlation coefficient normalizes covariance to a value between -1 and 1, so pairs with different units can be compared.

items.prompt: Two variables have negative covariance. Today X is over its average. What is likely true of Y?

options.label: Y is probably over its average
Y is probably below its average
Y is exactly at its average
Its position cannot be predicted

items.explain: With negative covariance, if X is above its expected value then Y is likely below its expected value.

items.prompt: Height is measured in meters and weight in kilograms. What units does their covariance have?

options.label: Meters divided by kilograms
No units, as it is a pure ratio
Meters times kilograms
Kilograms squared only

items.explain: The covariance of X and Y has the units of X times the units of Y.
